sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS TYPES OF VACATIONS AND TRIPS YOU ENJOY.  FIND OUT WHETHER THE OTHER CALLER CAN INTEREST YOU IN A VACATION SPOT YOU HAVEN'T VISITED.
turns: Yeah, I'm really into road trips, like hitting the coast or just driving nowhere in particular. What about you? Do you prefer camping or sticking to hotels?
Hotel it is. I've been sleeping in the back of a rig for three years, so the last thing I need is another cot in a dusty tent. I'd rather have a real bed and hot water. You?

Hot water is the only thing that matters, I've learned that the hard way. I got stuck in my car once on I-95 and spent three hours shivering while the temp dropped to zero. Then my buddy says, "Get out and walk it," and honestly, just getting my feet moving and seeing the snow on the ground actually warmed me up faster than any hotel room ever could. So yeah, I'm all about the roads and the fresh air, even if I do freeze a little bit.

Yeah, that actually reminds me of my cousin Dave who drives out to Colorado in the winter. He got stuck on a mountain pass last Christmas, too, and had to sit there for an hour waiting for a snowplow before he could move. Said he almost went hypothermic, but once the plow came by and cleared the lane, he just drove right through it. Kind of crazy how he just kept plugging away without panic.
That's wild, Dave sounds tough, but honestly the mountains are probably too sketchy for me; I'd rather just take the scenic byway down by the river and find some good barbecue spots.
I would love that, actually, I've never even been down there. Where exactly do you think it's at?

Oh, we're talking about the Blue Ridge Parkway, right? It's that long stretch up through the mountains near Asheville, North Carolina. There are these amazing overlooks with waterfalls, and if you time it right, you can hit the peaks when the air is crisp but the sun is still out. And there's this tiny town called Biltmore Village right off the road with these old, fancy-looking shops and places that serve really good food. You'd have to drive a couple hours to get there, but honestly, the views alone are worth the trip.
That sounds like a dream, honestly. I'd love to check out the waterfalls, but I'm worried about the gas mileage on a truck that big; do you think the views are worth paying for the extra fuel?
Yeah, definitely worth it, my cousin says he gets like fifty miles a gallon, but I'm thinking we could probably budget for it.

Yeah, fifty on a big rig is pretty good, and I'd be willing to pay a few extra bucks if it means seeing waterfalls that big from a moving truck instead of just staring at them through a window. Plus, you could probably stash the extra money in a travel fund for next time. What kind of food stuffs are you finding at that Biltmore place?

Well, they've got a spot that actually does breakfast in the shape of a giant cornucopia, but the real kicker is this one place right down the street where they serve up ribs that taste like they were smoked for a week straight.
Oh man, ribs sound perfect after sitting on the road all day, what kind of sauce do they put on them?
It's got a dry rub that pulls right out the fat, kind of sweet but not too sticky, and they put a little hickory smoke on it so it smells like a campfire inside the restaurant.
Yeah, sounds like the kind of sweet smoke that sticks to your ribs, I might just have to make a detour down there next time I'm heading north.
That hickory smoke stuff is kinda addictive, you know? Reminds me of how we cook here at the restaurant, but without the grease, so it's way easier on the stomach.
Yeah, that hickory smoke sounds legit, better than the restaurant version I guess, I might just pull over and grab a bite before I head back out to keep going.
Yeah, pull over, because if you're driving a truck you gotta make sure that joint's cold and the windows are cracked just enough so the smoke doesn't get stuck in the cab.
Yeah, good tip on cracking the window, I'll keep that in mind before I pull over to grab a bite.

Yeah, actually, you should put a little bag of ice in there with the ribs if you're worried about that heat building up in the cab, because if it gets too hot and you just run the AC on high, you're gonna lose all the smoke flavor anyway.
Yeah, that's a good call, I'll stash the ice in the cab so I don't sweat out all that hickory goodness while I'm driving.
That's the way to do it, keep the airflow going so the meat doesn't get steamed.
Yeah, that ice trick makes sense, I'll make sure to pack that before I hit the highway.
Yeah, just toss it in the cab with the ribs, and you're good to go.
Yeah, sounds like a solid plan, I'll grab a cooler for sure so I don't lose that smoke flavor once I'm back on the road.
Yeah, cooler is a smarter move than just a bag of ice, you'll want to keep it insulated for the whole drive back.
Yeah, I'll look into getting a cooler, might even grab one at the truck stop before I head out.
Yeah, that's a smart move, you'll definitely want the insulation so the meat stays cold on the long haul.
Yeah, I'll keep that in mind, maybe I'll grab one at the truck stop before I head out.

Yeah, go ahead and pick one up, maybe even get the lid that locks so the meat doesn't get squished, but I'll tell you what, if you wanna keep that hickory flavor fresh, you gotta keep the AC on low and the windows cracked so the fumes don't ruin the meat, and hey, have you ever thought about taking a train trip instead? It's way smoother than sitting behind the wheel for days, plus you can actually stand up and stretch out your legs without worrying about the cab getting stuffy or the engine getting hot.
That train thing sounds pretty tempting actually, maybe I should try that once the weather gets a little nicer.
Yeah, and honestly, sitting on a train is just way less stressful than being in a cage for eight hours, plus you can actually look at the scenery instead of watching the road.
Yeah, I can see why, train sounds way smoother than being locked in a cab, but I gotta admit, I've never actually taken one, just always stuck to the road.
Yeah, I've never taken one myself, but if you ever do, you gotta tell me which route you picked.
Yeah, I'd love to hear which route you'd pick, but honestly I think I'll stick to the road for now since I know every inch of the interstate.
Yeah, stick to the road for now, man. You know that highway rhythm better than anyone.
Yeah, sticking to the road is my life, but I'm open to a train ride if it means I can actually get some real sleep without the engine humming in my ear.

Yeah, if you do decide to hop on the rails, I'd say hop aboard the Amtrak Acela between DC and Boston; it's the only line that's actually fast enough to make a train trip feel like a road trip instead of a prison sentence.
Yeah, the Acela sounds legit if it's actually worth the extra cash compared to just grabbing a rental.

Yeah, if you think about the cost, the Acela might eat up your whole trip budget just on tickets alone, so maybe you'll find a better deal on the regular lines or just stick to the road for the price.
Yeah, I guess if the Acela is that pricey, I'll just stick to the road and maybe find a decent motel along the way instead.
